problem_text:
A logistics manager is assembling a shipment of specialized components to maximize total utility while adhering to a cargo weight restriction.

The components under consideration are:
* Component A: weight 39kg, utility 99 credits
* Component B: weight 47kg, utility 122 credits
* Component C: weight 42kg, utility 290 credits
* Component D: weight 7kg, utility 25 credits
* Component E: weight 3kg, utility 211 credits
* Component F: weight 26kg, utility 154 credits
* Component G: weight 11kg, utility 204 credits
* Component H: weight 2kg, utility 173 credits
* Component I: weight 41kg, utility 225 credits
* Component J: weight 34kg, utility 112 credits
* Component K: weight 33kg, utility 192 credits
* Component L: weight 39kg, utility 135 credits
* Component M: weight 44kg, utility 26 credits
* Component N: weight 27kg, utility 262 credits
* Component O: weight 33kg, utility 34 credits
* Component P: weight 13kg, utility 183 credits
* Component Q: weight 30kg, utility 104 credits
* Component R: weight 37kg, utility 110 credits
* Component S: weight 14kg, utility 28 credits
* Component T: weight 13kg, utility 71 credits
* Component U: weight 19kg, utility 175 credits
* Component V: weight 22kg, utility 166 credits

Furthermore, due to compatibility requirements, precisely one of Component A and Component B must be included in the shipment.

If Component C is included, the permissible gross cargo weight is effectively diminished by 10 kg.
The transport vehicle can accommodate a maximum of 403 kg. The manager must determine the optimal selection of components.
